slides.title: It is appropriate for the nurse to delegate to a UAP the
text: It is appropriate for the nurse to delegate to a UAP the
taking of vital signs for which of the following clients?
A client being prepared for elective facial surgery with a history of stable hypertension.
A client receiving a blood transfusion with a history of transfusion reactions.
A client recently started on a new antiarrhythmic agent.
A client who is admitted frequently with asthma attacks.

slides.title: A client being prepared for elective facial surgery with a history of stable hypertension. Yes, the client is stable.
text: A client being prepared for elective facial surgery with a history of stable hypertension. Yes, the client is stable.
A client receiving a blood transfusion with a history of transfusion reactions. No, this client is unstable.
A client recently started on a new antiarrhythmic agent. No, the UAP can not take apical pulses.
A client who is admitted frequently with asthma attacks. No, This client is unstable and vital signs measurement cannot be delegated.

slides.title: Vital Signs
text: TPR & BP ( ALWAYS IN THIS ORDER)- pain the fifth VS
Measurement of vital signs provides data
to determine a client's state of health
Possible change in physiological function & need for medical or nursing intervention
Should be a thoughtful, scientific assessment, not a routine job that you never look at!!!!

slides.title: Vital Signs
text: Pre and post medication administration that could affect CV( cardiovascular) system
Per agency policy or HCP order
Even when there is an order for how often to take vitals, they can be taken when the nurse feels it is important
Client must be stable and not a new admission to delegate this task!!

slides.title: Vital SignsBody Temperature
text: Balance between heat produced & heat loss  = body temp
Shivering-involuntary response to temperature differences in body

slides.title: Infants
text: Newborns must be kept warm to prevent hypothermia
Tympanic or temporal artery sites preferred
Tends to be lower than that of middle-aged adults

slides.title: Never take an oral temperature on unconscious client, seizure client,  combative or uncooperative
text: Never take an oral temperature on unconscious client, seizure client,  combative or uncooperative
Do not use tympanic thermometer on someone w/ infected ear, lesion, incision or hearing aide
Stay w/ client during the procedure
Rectal temps may change heart rate

slides.title: Vital SignsPyrexia
text: Dehydration, rapid heart rate, decreased urinary output
infectious diseases triggered by; viruses, bacteria, fungi, or parasites

slides.title: Vital Signs
text: Monitor laboratory results for signs of dehydration or infection
Remove excess blankets when client feels warm
Provide adequate nutrition and fluid (up to 3L/day)
Provide dry clothing and bed linens

slides.title: Vital SignsHypothermia
text: Heat loss due to prolonged exposure to cold
Uncontrolled shivering, memory loss, depression, poor judgment

slides.title: Vital SignsFrost Bite
text: Occurs when body is exposed to extreme temperatures and ice crystals form in cells
May cause permanent tissue or circulatory damage
Ear lobes, fingers, toes, tip of nose

slides.title: Occurs when profuse diaphoresis causes water & electrolyte loss
text: Occurs when profuse diaphoresis causes water & electrolyte loss
Prolonged exposure to sun or high environment temps
Heat emergency with high mortality rate
Victims may not sweat because of hypothalamus damage

slides.title: Vital SignsPulse
text: Pulse rate = number of beats per minute (BPM)
Volume of blood pumped by heart in one minute = cardiac output (CO)

slides.title: Vital SignsAssessment of pulse
text: If either one of these are detected. Must check apical pulse!!!
Rate= how many beats per minute
Rhythm= pattern of beats equal or not, hence regular or irregular, if skipped or uneven beats its irregular
Volume= pulse strength, absent, weak, normal, bounding
Bilateral equality= equal on both sides
Radial or brachial pulse may be delegated to UAP

slides.title: Vital SignsRespirations
text: Mechanism body uses to exchange gases between atmosphere and blood/cells
Passive controlled by respiratory center in the brain - Medulla Oblongata
Ventilation is regulated by CO2 levels

slides.title: Vital SignsRespiratory Assessment
text: Begins with the act of breathing

slides.title: Bradypnea
text: Anatomic and physiologic changes cause respiratory system to be less efficient

slides.title: Vital Signs
text: Detects hypoxemia before clinical signs and symptoms

slides.title: Vital SignsBlood Pressure
text: The lateral force on walls of artery by the pulsing blood under pressure by the heart

slides.title: Vital Signs
text: Pulse Pressure = difference between systolic and diastolic pressures
A rise or fall of 20-30 mm Hg is significant

slides.title: Vital SignsHypertension
text: Systolic 2 or more > 140 mmHg; or 130 mmHg if DM or renal
Diastolic readings 2 or more > 90 mm Hg

slides.title: Systolic below 90 mm Hg
text: Occurs r/t dilation of the arteries in vascular bed, loss of blood volume, or heart pump failure
- Postural hypotension - drop in systolic blood pressure upon standing of >

slides.title: Feeling dizzy or lightheaded
text: Changes in vision such as blurring
Pain across the back of shoulders and neck
Pain in lower back and buttocks
Instruct client to change position slowly
Sit down immediately to prevent falls
A fall in blood pressure leads to a reduced blood supply to organs and muscles

slides.title: A client has a total serum calcium level of 7.6mg/dL. Which clinical manifestations should the nurse expect to note on assessment of the client? Select all that apply.
text: A client has a total serum calcium level of 7.6mg/dL. Which clinical manifestations should the nurse expect to note on assessment of the client? Select all that apply.
Prolonged ST interval and QT interval on EKG.

slides.title: Constipation. No, client would have diarrhea.
text: Constipation. No, client would have diarrhea.
Muscle twitching. Yes, a sign of hypocalcemia.
Hypoactive bowel sounds. No, bowel sounds would be hyperactive.
Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes. Yes, a sign of hypocalcemia.
Positive Trousseaus and Chvostek sign. Yes, a sign of hypocalcemia.
Prolonged ST interval and QT interval on EKG. Yes, a sign of hypocalcemia.

slides.title: Intravenous Site
text: What steps should the nurse include when starting an IV?
Place protective towel/pad under client's arm.
Apply tourniquet 3-4 inches above selected site
Client must hold arm lower than the heart and open and close fist several times
Cleanse area with antiseptic solution (back-and forth) and allow to air dry
Hold skin taunt 1-2 inches below the entry site
Enter skin, bevel side up, holding the hub of the catheter at a 10-15-degree angle

slides.title: IV Complications
text: Leakage of intravenous solution into surrounding tissue
Edema, coldness, pain around infusion site, decrease in flow rate
Blood clot in a vein, causing inflammation
Inflammation of the wall of a vein
Local tenderness, redness, warmth, edema above the insertion site
Caused by poor infection control, long term catheter insertion, contaminated IV fluid, poor insertion techniques, multiple attempts at insertion

slides.title: IV Complications
text: Too large a volume of fluid infuses into the circulatory system
Engorged neck veins, increased BP, dyspnea
Respiratory distress, increased heart rate, cyanosis, decreased blood pressure change in LOC
Body's reaction to a substance injected to the circulatory system too rapidly
Pounding headache, fainting, rapid pulse, chills, dyspnea, back pain
Leakage of vesicant intravenous solution into surrounding tissue

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Case Study
text: The nurse in the heart failure clinic is caring for a 72-year-old male client who is taking prescribed furosemide. The client appears drowsy and is confused with place and time. The client states, “I feel weak and tired all of the time.” The client’s spouse reports the client forgot to take their morning dose of furosemide yesterday and “doubled the dose to play catch up about 24 hours ago.” The client has not been themself per the spouse’s report. The client has numbness and tingling in the hands with weak hand grasps bilaterally and reports feeling tired. The client is compliant with a low-fat diet, but their appetite is poor today. Vital signs: temperature (T) 99.0° F, pulse (P) 100, respirations (R) 12 and shallow, blood pressure (BP) 110/78 mm Hg, and pulse oximetry (SpO2) 96% on room air.
Based on the documentation presented in the nursing note above, which of the following findings would require immediate follow-up by the nurse?
